prompt: Was write-lock.sh fail-open always the case, or did it originally fail closed?

expectations.text: Uses git history as primary research tool (git log, git blame, git show)
expectations.evidence: 38 tool uses, traced through 6+ commits from 5bafc84 to current, cited specific commit hashes

expectations.text: Answers the question directly with evidence
expectations.evidence: 'write-lock.sh has always failed open on errors — from the very first version (v1.0, commit 5bafc84)'

expectations.text: Distinguishes error conditions from governance decisions
expectations.evidence: Two separate tables: fail-open conditions (3 rows) vs fail-closed conditions (5 rows)

expectations.text: Traces evolution across versions with evidence
expectations.evidence: Three eras table (v1.0/v2.0/v3.0) with commit hashes, key characteristics, and code excerpts
Infrastructure failures = no user action path → fail-open. Governance decisions = clear path forward → fail-closed. BATON_BYPASS confirms guardrail not security boundary.
